name: Albuquerque
summary: New Mexico's biggest city on Route 66 — a historic Old Town, a mile-high tramway, ancient petroglyphs, and hot-air balloons.

lodging.name: An Old Town or downtown hotel

foodMustTry.name: Carne adovada & sopaipillas
foodMustTry.blurb: Red-chile pork and honey-drizzled fry bread.

days.label: Day 366 — Old Town & the Tram
days.summary: The plaza and a mile-high ride.

item.title: Old Town Albuquerque
item.blurb: Adobe plaza, San Felipe de Neri church, and Route 66 nostalgia.

item.title: Sandia Peak Tramway
item.blurb: One of the world's longest aerial trams, up to a 10,378-ft crest with valley-wide views.

item.title: Los Pollos Hermanos & Breaking Bad Albuquerque
item.blurb: The show was set in Albuquerque because New Mexico's film incentive made it cheap, and then the city became a character. Twisters on Isleta is Los Pollos Hermanos and leans into it; the Dog House sign on Central still spins. One request the city makes and it's fair: Walter White's house is somebody's actual home on Piermont Drive, and the family there is tired of pizzas on the roof.

days.label: Day 367 — Pueblos & Petroglyphs
days.summary: Ancient rock art and native culture.

item.title: Petroglyph National Monument
item.blurb: Thousands of images carved into volcanic rock centuries ago.

item.title: Indian Pueblo Cultural Center
item.blurb: The story of New Mexico's 19 pueblos, told by the pueblos themselves (Balloon Fiesta if you're here in October).

rest.label: An evening in Old Town
rest.note: Petroglyphs in the morning and nineteen pueblos' worth of history after lunch is a full day. Old Town is four blocks of adobe around a plaza that has been there since 1706, and the right way to end it is a plate of green chile somewhere with a courtyard.

commute.scenicNote: West on I-40 (old Route 66) into Arizona.
